ground_truth.description: The added test is titled/scoped to the pre-existing snapshot contract (_known_projects frozen at init) and does not assert anything about the actual behavior change in this diff — the once-per-process discoverability log (_registry_log_emitted). The new logging code path is instantiated but never verified (e.g. via caplog), so the diff's real change is untested.

The comment asserts that because 'the proj_a orchestrator lock doesn't exist' the escalation is skipped, but tick() on a failed ticket can actually emit an escalation_created event (unintended side effect). The test passes on the _known_projects assertion while silently triggering escalation machinery, meaning the stated rationale for why tick() is safe here is unverified and likely incorrect.

_registry_log_emitted is a mutable class-level flag set once per process and never reset. In the test suite (which constructs many janitors), any test that tries to assert the init log was emitted becomes order-dependent/flaky, since an earlier-constructed janitor in the session already flipped the flag to True.

provenance.runs_db_query: SELECT task_id, project_id, outcome, review_cycles, verify_attempts FROM task_results WHERE review_cycles >= 1, cross-referenced with events (escalation_created, merge_finalized) -- see mining.mine_fn_candidates.
